summary: Adds a new opcode to the SSH terminal modes encoding for the widely used IUTF8 mode. It indicates that the terminal input and output use UTF-8 text.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8160 adds an SSH terminal-mode opcode for IUTF8. It lets a client tell the server that terminal input and output use UTF-8, which can affect how the server handles line editing.

questions: what is ssh terminal mode opcode 42
what does ssh terminal mode opcode 42 mean
subtitle: A new SSH terminal mode for indicating that terminal input and output use UTF-8.

tldr.problem: SSH terminal-mode encoding lacked a value for the commonly used IUTF8 setting that tells a terminal driver how to handle UTF-8 input.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns opcode 42 to IUTF8, followed by a 32-bit value where 0 disables the mode and 1 enables it.
tldr.outcome: An SSH client can report the terminal mode during a pseudo-terminal request, and the server may ignore it.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 8160's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC adds IUTF8 to SSH's encoded terminal modes.

sections.title: Why SSH Needs an IUTF8 Mode
sections.content:
The SSH connection protocol carries terminal modes when requesting a pseudo-terminal. IUTF8 is a commonly used mode bit that indicates terminal input and output use UTF-8 character encoding.

A server's terminal driver can use this information to decide how many input bytes form one logical character during line editing. SSH previously had no encoded terminal mode for IUTF8.
sections.plainLanguage: The server may need to know whether terminal text uses UTF-8. That information helps it handle multibyte characters during line editing.

sections.title: Opcode 42 and Its Value
sections.content:
The RFC assigns opcode 42 to the IUTF8 terminal mode. The opcode is followed by a 32-bit value: 0 means the mode is disabled, and 1 means it is enabled.

A client should send a value when it knows the mode. The server may ignore the value, as it may ignore other encoded terminal modes.
sections.plainLanguage: The client sends opcode 42 with a value that says whether IUTF8 is off or on. The server can use the setting or ignore it.

sections.title: Handling UTF-8 Input Carefully
sections.content:
The RFC says the added mode has no security implications different from the other SSH terminal modes. It also says that UTF-8 security considerations apply when IUTF8 is enabled.

Terminal drivers using the mode for UTF-8-aware line editing should consider how they handle illegal sequences, overlong encodings, and redundant representations of composed characters.
sections.plainLanguage: Turning on UTF-8-aware editing requires careful handling of invalid or unusual UTF-8 sequences. The RFC points to the existing SSH and UTF-8 security considerations.
